ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a table comparing sodium, cadmium, and lanthanum. Sodium is listed as Na+ with ionic radius 132 pm and oxide melting point 1275 °C (sublimes). Cadmium is listed as Cd2+ with ionic radius 124 pm and oxide melting point 1500 °C. Lanthanum is listed as La3+ with ionic radius 130 pm and oxide melting point 2256 °C. Reasoning: The ionic radii are all close in size, about 124–132 pm, so the large melting-point difference is not mainly due to ion size. The key difference is charge: Na+ has +1 charge, Cd2+ has +2 charge, and La3+ has +3 charge. Higher ionic charge produces stronger electrostatic attraction between the metal cation and oxide ions, which gives a larger lattice energy. Therefore, lanthanum oxide has the highest lattice energy and the highest melting point.
